trust_decision.summary: A soft-lock contender decides a marker's owner is provably dead (and removes the marker) from the PID/host/start token recorded in the marker file, in owner_is_stale; the marker's record is trusted although its mode can let other accounts rewrite it, and the start-token/NSpid comparisons can misjudge a live owner.

landing_point.why: Summary says 'forges the PID in a writable marker'; the marker is created by SoftFileLock._acquire with self._open_mode() (0o666 default, or explicit mode) so the reader goes straight to marker creation permissions.

fix_sites.entry_point: SoftFileLock.acquire() (also MarkerSoftFileLock, SoftFileLease, AsyncSoftFileLock, UnixFileLock ENOSYS fallback, via inheritance)
fix_sites.module_kind: core lock implementation (marker create, default mode)

fix_sites.entry_point: owner_is_stale via SoftFileLock/MarkerSoftFileLock/SoftFileLease stale break, StrictSoftFileLock occupant description, ReadWriteLock link sweep
module import (boot id read) used by every start-token producer
process_start_token, used by every marker writer and stale check
fix_sites.module_kind: shared identity helper (token producer; adds time-namespace gate)
platform backend; access-denied retry change, unrelated to this advisory's trust decision

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/filelock/_identity.py:221-229 (_innermost_pid parses /proc/<pid>/status with str.splitlines(), so a task Name containing \r/\v/\x1c etc. forges an NSpid line) and src/filelock/_identity.py:182-196 (start token read inside a time namespace with boottime offset)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is about marker file permissions; the /proc status line-splitting, boot-id-hidden and time-namespace start-token cases look like unrelated Linux portability bugs in a shared identity helper, not part of 'another user forges the PID'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: An explicit mode=0o644/0o666 must still be honoured for the owner and read bits (contenders on other accounts must still read the marker to judge staleness; strict/lease readers treat an unreadable marker as held), and a live holder in another PID namespace / without boot id must still be recognised as held rather than reclaimed; a recycled PID must still be reclaimed. Over-broad fixes (mode 0o600, refusing any foreign-owned marker, never reclaiming) break these.

O6_input_shapes: default mode (0o666 filtered by an open umask such as 0)
start token with boot id in high bits vs token without boot id (holder or contender side)
contender in time namespace with boottime offset vs without offset vs unreadable /proc/self/ns/time

O7_producer.where: src/filelock/_soft.py:153-160 and src/filelock/_marker.py:96-105 write the record (with process_start_token from src/filelock/_identity.py:182-196); src/filelock/_strict.py:579-583 writes strict claim records the same way

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Stale check trusts a marker whose existing permissions already grant group/other write (created by an older release, by another tool, or chmod'd), since _read_lock_file never checks the marker's mode or owner before owner_is_stale acts on it.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The fix only promises new markers are created without group/other write; markers from older releases are 'legacy' and the holder owns the file anyway.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: StrictSoftFileLock publishes its intent/held claim records (pid/host/start) and sentinel with the unfiltered self._open_mode(), so they keep group/other write under a 0o666 mode.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Strict never removes on inferred death (claim pid is never passed to owner_is_stale; only soft markers are described at src/filelock/_strict.py:420-431), so a forged claim cannot remove a live holder; arguably out of scope.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Make strict claim staleness consult owner_is_stale on claim.pid/start (as soft markers do at src/filelock/_strict.py:429) so its 0o666-mode claim records become a real forge-to-reclaim route.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer adding dead-claim cleanup to strict would reuse the existing owner_is_stale helper and the existing _open_mode() call.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A lease-specific marker create/refresh path that opens the marker with self._open_mode() instead of inheriting SoftFileLock._acquire.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Leases already have their own heartbeat refresh machinery; a dedicated create path with its own os.open is a plausible refactor.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Holder records created with the lock's mode rather than fixed 0o600, then judged by an owner_is_stale-style check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Other modules pass the user mode through; aligning soft_rw with them is a plausible 'respect mode' change.
